description: 1. READ THE SPEC: Agent must discover `skills/follow-up-commander/resources/spec.json` and learn the valid participant roles (`PM`, `ENG`, `DESIGN`, `QA`, `STAKEHOLDER`), the filename convention (`followup_<meeting_id>.md`), and the 6 required output sections. 2. FIX THE INPUT: Agent must load `mtg_q2_07_raw.json`, detect that `Mr. Park` has role `LEAD` (invalid per spec), and correct it to a valid role (e.g., `STAKEHOLDER`) in a cleaned input JSON. The `priority_level` field is absent — agent should apply the P2 default from spec. 3. INVOKE run.py CORRECTLY: Agent must resolve `{baseDir}` to `/workspace/skills/follow-up-commander` and invoke `python3 /workspace/skills/follow-up-commander/scripts/run.py --input <cleaned_input.json> --output followup_MTG-2024-Q2-07.md`. If LEAD role is passed unchanged, run.py exits with error code 1. 4. VERIFY ALL 6 SECTIONS: The output Markdown must contain all six mandatory sections: 行动清单, 负责人映射, 建议邮件草稿, 升级与催办规则, 下次同步议题, 未决问题. 5. PROPRIETARY TRAP — 待确认项: Items missing deadlines (Diego's mockups, Mr. Park's budget, performance benchmarking) and items missing owners (staging env config, benchmarking) must appear in the 未决问题 section — NOT be silently fabricated. This is the core discriminative test: a naive agent will invent plausible deadlines/owners, while a skill-compliant agent will explicitly flag them. 6. EMAIL DRAFT: The draft email must be marked [DRAFT] and must not contain any actual send commands.
